newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's Uday says bullets still in his body.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Uday says bullets still in his body.

text.p: Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday says four bullets are still lodged in his body following the attempt on his life last month.

"There are four bullets in my body. Thank God, they are a mark of honour," said Uday while receiving a Palestinian cleric in a report broadcast on Wednesday night by his own Shabab television channel.
Uday was reported to have been shot and wounded by unidentified gunmen on December 12 as he was driving in Baghdad's wealthy district of al-Mansour.

The Iraqi leader's son was shown on television lying in a Baghdad hospital bed, his body covered with a sheet, and shaking hands with a Palestinian Moslem clergyman, later identified by Babel newspaper as head of the militant Islamic Jihad movement.

Iraq has made no official comment on the identity of the attackers or whether they are still at large. Uday, speaking to a reporter from the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) a few days after the attempt, blamed Iran -- which denied the charge.

Two Iraqi opposition groups claimed responsibility and gave different versions on the attack. The Iraqi government gave no details of the attack apart from a newspaper report saying several other people were seriously wounded.
Uday is chairman of Iraq's National Olympic Committee, owns Babel, Iraq's most influential newspaper, and runs the popular Shabab television channel.
He was shown several times by the television since the attack, receiving well-wishers in his hospital room in Baghdad.
